clue.text: Note emissions — liquids not to be sniffed?

parts.note: sol (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
vents are outlets, things let out or discharged, so emissions

explanation.surface: A musical note's emissions turn out to be fumes that nobody should breathe in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on glue- and solvent-sniffing: these are liquids whose fumes should not be inhaled.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvents such as glue thinners give off intoxicating vapours, and inhaling them is a notorious form of substance abuse.

clue.text: A lark's in rambling country

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters of the words before it are set wandering into a new order

explanation.surface: A skylark goes wandering across the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rambling' shuffles A, LARKS and IN (the possessive 's counting as an S here) into the island nation's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation off the southern tip of India.

clue.text: Runs taking gradient, top to bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the top letter of the word for gradient is moved down to the bottom

parts.note: a slope is an incline or gradient

explanation.surface: A runner tackles a hill, with the instruction to go from summit to foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top to bottom' moves the S of SLOPE from the start to the end, giving LOPES.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy strides, so lopes means runs.

clue.text: The French chaps in film? I may be one

indicators.note: in here means one piece is placed inside the name of the film

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about a stranded alien
le is the French masculine word for 'the'
chaps are men

explanation.surface: French men appearing in a movie, with a cryptic aside from the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I may be one' looks like a personal remark; I is the chemical symbol for iodine, which is one of the chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: Iodine, symbol I, is a chemical substance in the periodic table, so I is an example of one.

clue.text: Huge woman, not half a tragic one

indicators.note: not half means the first half of the word for a huge woman is dropped, leaving the other half

parts.note: a giantess is a female giant, a huge woman

explanation.surface: A large woman, though only half the size of a famously doomed one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'woman'. Tess of the d'Urbervilles is the tragic heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's heroine Tess Durbeyfield meets a doomed end, making her the classic tragic woman of English fiction.

clue.text: Surly guy heartlessly grabbing what's left

indicators.note: grabbing means the outer letters take hold of another piece placed between them
heartlessly means the middle of the word guy is removed, keeping only its first and last letters

parts.note: a rump is a remnant, the part that is left over

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered man heartlessly snatches whatever remains.
explanation.walkthrough: G and Y, the first and last letters of 'guy', grab RUMP between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy and surly both describe someone bad-tempered and sullen.

clue.text: Part of boat to sway when bird enters

indicators.note: enters means the bird goes inside the word for sway

parts.note: to rock is to sway to and fro
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A boat starts to rock when a bird lands aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal; 'when' is only a link. A rowlock is the oar fitting, not a lock on the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowlock is the fitting on a boat's gunwale that holds an oar in place.

clue.text: Fellow that redeveloped an area in new York

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: redeveloped suggests property rebuilt, so the letters of the word that are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A man who rebuilt a district of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' turns THAT into HATT. 'new York' is lower-cased so that 'new' could pass as an anagram signal; it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manhattan is the central borough of New York City.

clue.text: You get sun in hot country? We can't disagree!

indicators.note: in here means the letter for sun is placed inside the name of the country

parts.note: Yemen is a hot Middle Eastern country
S is the abbreviation for sun (as in Sunday)

explanation.surface: Sunshine guaranteed in a hot country, and nobody will argue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'You get' is link padding. The definition is what such people would say: they never contradict their boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Yes men are sycophants who always agree with their superiors, so they can never voice dissent.

clue.text: Troubled by spiders, me? Overpowered!

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of the words that follow are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened arachnophobe says that spiders get the better of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troubled' rearranges SPIDERS and ME. 'Overpowered' is the old sense of pressing into service.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to force someone into service, as press gangs did with sailors, so impressed means seized by force.

clue.text: Place of crime, a little bit run down

parts.note: a den, as in a den of thieves or iniquity, is a place where crime goes on
an ounce is a small amount, as in 'not an ounce of sense'

explanation.surface: A crime scene in a slightly run-down condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run down' looks like a description of a shabby place, but it is the verb meaning to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To run something down is to disparage it; to denounce is to condemn it publicly.

clue.text: Needs workers to join wife

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers

explanation.surface: A firm needs staff to work alongside the boss's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Wants and needs are both nouns for things required or lacked.

clue.text: Author in a university, not one of the big guns

parts.words: not one of the big guns
parts.note: the Sten is a light submachine gun, so not a big gun

explanation.surface: A writer at a university who is not one of the leading figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big guns' looks like 'important people'; the Sten was a light British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen is the English novelist who wrote Pride and Prejudice.

clue.text: Gloss woman's brought to old gallery

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name; the 's stands for 'is' and gives no letters
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A woman is brought along to a long-established art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: THE TATE is London's famous group of art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To gloss a text is to add explanatory notes or comments to it.

clue.text: Demanded a lot of paper, looking embarrassed about it

indicators.note: about means the word for embarrassed goes round the paper measure

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Someone asked for a big stack of paper and blushed about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal: the colour of a blush goes around the paper measure. A quire is a printer's quantity of 24 or 25 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Required means asked for as necessary or obligatory, as in demanded.

clue.text: Express frustration while mopping up? The last thing you'll do

explanation.surface: A cleaner kicks over the pail in anger, then a grim reminder of mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a literal scene of a cleaner kicking a pail; the second is the slang idiom for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, kicking over a pail in annoyance while cleaning; idiomatically, the phrase means to die, the final act of anyone's life.

clue.text: Paper suggesting that a policy has yet to be formulated?

definitions.text: Paper suggesting that a policy has yet to be formulated?

parts.words: Paper suggesting that a policy has yet to be formulated
parts.note: reads like a political discussion document, but means an insurance document giving temporary protection until the full policy is issued

explanation.walkthrough: 'policy' suggests government policy; here it is an insurance policy.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer issues this temporary certificate of insurance while the actual policy document is still being prepared.

clue.text: Altering incorrect figure

indicators.note: incorrect tells us the word altering is set down wrongly, its letters in another order

explanation.surface: Changing a wrong number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incorrect' rearranges ALTERING. 'figure' suggests a number, but it is a geometrical shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Calm avenue cur fouled up — something needed to clean up mess

definitions.text: something needed to clean up mess

indicators.note: fouled up means messed up, so the letters of the three words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A dog has fouled a quiet street, and someone must clean up the mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fouled up' rearranges CALM, AVENUE and CUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum cleaner is a household appliance that sucks up dirt and dust.

clue.text: Biblical place's volunteers joined in game

parts.note: Cana is the Galilee town where Jesus turned water into wine; the possessive gives CANA'S
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers from a Bible town join in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive's S counts as a letter. The TA (Territorial Army) is Britain's part-time volunteer army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game played with two packs.

clue.text: Suffer humiliation being badly attired

indicators.note: badly means done wrongly, so the letters of attired are put together the wrong way

explanation.surface: Someone is mortified at being poorly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges ATTIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat dirt is an idiom for having to accept humiliation or grovel.

clue.text: Peg is a greedy person being embraced by a drunkard

indicators.note: being embraced by means the greedy person is held inside the drunkard

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
a pig is a glutton, a greedy person

explanation.surface: A glutton gets a hug from a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being embraced by' is the container signal: the glutton is hugged by the drunkard. 'Peg' is the definition, a cask plug.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is a small peg or plug used to stop the vent hole of a cask.

clue.text: North and south?

parts.note: looks like two compass points or regions, but refers to two seats at a bridge table, who play as a team

explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, players are named by compass points; North and South play together.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the players sitting North and South form one team against East and West.

clue.text: Superior hat, a solution to all our problems?

parts.note: U stands for upper class, socially superior
a topi is a sun helmet, a pith hat

explanation.surface: A fancy hat presented as the answer to everything.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class (superior) speech and manners. A TOPI is a pith helmet worn in hot countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is an imagined perfect society in which every difficulty has been resolved.

clue.text: Cause of disease in jail Sweden avoided

indicators.note: avoided means the letter for Sweden is left out of the word for jail

parts.note: a prison is a jail
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A Swede manages to escape a jail sentence because of illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from PRISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A prion is a misfolded protein that causes brain diseases such as BSE and CJD.

clue.text: American Indian's beliefs not totally formulated

indicators.note: not totally formulated means the word is left incomplete, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a creed is a set of religious beliefs

explanation.surface: A Native American people's faith is still only half worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letter of CREED. 'American Indian's' is read as 'American Indian is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cree are a First Nations people of Canada and the northern United States.

clue.text: Fools don't stop, having succeeded

parts.note: go on means continue, don't stop
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Idiots keep going and somehow come out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: S for 'succeeded' appears in family trees and lists of monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: Goons are stupid or clownish people.

clue.text: One line I found in terrible danger, this action becoming possibility?

indicators.note: found in means the three letters are placed inside the scrambled word
terrible signals the letters of danger are made into a mess

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: With a railway line in grave danger, a crash becomes a real prospect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns DANGER into DERANG; 'found in' puts ILI inside it. The definition leans on the surface: a line in danger makes this happening to a train possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Derailing is the accident of a train leaving its rails, which a damaged track makes a real prospect.

clue.text: Article by graduate has name of old city

parts.note: the is the definite article
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece by a graduate names an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word; 'of old city' is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Theban means belonging to Thebes, an ancient city of Greece and also of Egypt.

clue.text: Bird that comes to a full stop

definitions.text: that comes to a full stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is British slang for a prison term, from rhyming slang 'birdlime', time.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird is British slang (from rhyming slang 'birdlime' = time) for a prison term; a written grammatical unit ends with a full stop.
